The six lexical termini of the poem are

mountains – valleys – forests – music – morning – evening

and they are worked through the whole piece in the normal
retrograde sestina permutation

1 2 3 4 5 6
6 1 5 2 4 3
3 6 4 1 2 5
5 3 2 6 1 4
4 5 1 3 6 2
2 4 6 5 3 1
…

normal tornada the six termini have to be present, three of them
as line-final and three in the middle of the three lines.  In the
text as printed

73 These mountains witness shall, so shall these valleys;   1+2
74 Long since, alas, my deadly swannish music               4
75 Our morning hymn is this, and song at evening.          5+6

are present but 3 forests is absent.  Line 74 is the only tornada
line that can be changed without destroying the final-word
sestina chain, because it is line-final in music. The only line in

contains forests in the middle of the line is

25 These forests eke, made wretched by our music;

disturbing the end-word permutation of the 12 sestina stanzas.

normal envoi

73 mountains + valleys
74 forests + music
75 morning + evening

and restores the 1–2–3–4–5–6 tornada.  In the printed text 25 and
